reasons: Scale: the beads read about 40-48% oversize against both stated body referents (brief rule 4). Just above the bracelet the wrist measures 311 px across (skin edges x661 and x972 at y1650), and the forearm just below it measures 337 px (y1850). Front beads measure 49-50 px (for example the first large bead right of the ring, x909-958, y1753-1801). With the wrist at 55 mm that gives 8.0-8.8 mm per bead, about 8.5 mm or +38% to +46% against 6 mm. The most frontal fingernail (ring finger, around x640-700, y255-340) is about 55 px wide; at 10 mm that gives 8.9 mm (+48%). The beads are 0.9 of a nail wide; the prompt asked for half a nail.

Cross-check against the listing's own on-wrist photos: beads are 0.10 of the wrist width in listing-3 and 0.105 in listing-5, against 0.15-0.16 here. The heart is 0.18-0.19 of the wrist width there, against 0.28-0.30 here. The whole bracelet sits about 1.5x larger on the wrist than the real piece, so it reads chunky and a shopper would expect a bolder bracelet than they get. The 12 large beads plus clasp visible across the front would also need a bracelet of about 25 cm at this scale, not 18 cm.
notes: Construction matches listing-1/4. Bar side: small bead, silver link, gold jump ring, then a straight flat-ended polished T-bar threaded through the ring, with its loop showing under the bar. Ring side: gold jump ring at about 2-3 o'clock, silver link, small bead, then the strand. There is exactly one smooth, puffed, polished heart on a gold jump ring at 6 o'clock. Nothing is melted at phone size.

Heart is 92 px wide (x752-844), about 15.1-16.6 mm by wrist or nail (+1% to +11% against 15 mm), so it is on the brief's number. Heart to bead is 1.85, the same as every listing photo (1.8-1.95). The piece's own proportions are faithful; only its absolute size on the body is wrong. Note: with the real 1.85 ratio, the brief's 15 mm heart and 6 mm bead cannot both hold. The listing on-wrist photos put the real heart at about 10.5-11 mm wide.
Worn frame, so the full count cannot be checked. 12 large beads (6 each side) plus both small end beads show across the front, consistent with 23.

Beads read as polished mid-grey steel. They carry hard-edged mirror reflections of the skin and crisp white highlights, with mean luminance 108-144 against 122-143 on the listing-1/4 beads. They do not read as pearl, matte or hematite.

Hand: five digits. Thumb at the right (tip about x1065,y740), index pointing up-right, middle finger curled behind with only its tip showing between ring and index (about x650-700, y620-650), ring finger straight up, little finger straight up. Order, joints, creases and bare nails are natural. The back of the hand faces the camera (the prompt asked for the palm), and the curled middle finger reads as a mudra. Fingers are long against the slender wrist (ring finger about 660 px from the web, about 115 mm at wrist scale), an elongated dancer's hand. It is not deformed at phone size, so this is a note, not a fail.
Face scan: all four edges and the dupatta folds were checked. No eye, brow, lash, nose, lips, mouth, chin or jaw anywhere, and no shoulder.
No text, logos, rings, henna, watch or second bracelet.
The piece sits where it really would: below the wrist joint, toggle on top, heart hanging toward the elbow under gravity.
Palette is on-brand: dusty blush plaster wall (hue about 16 deg, saturation 0.2) and blush chiffon, with a calm top third for the headline.
Ad quality once the scale is fixed would be about 8.2. Elegant and calm, but the bracelet is small in a 9:16 frame and the gesture reads as a graceful hand more than Kathak.
fix: Keep the wall, dupatta, light and bracelet construction, but set scale by the beads and the wrist, not the heart. Replace the worn scale line with: 'a fine, delicate strand: each bead about half the width of her fingernail and about one tenth of the width of her wrist; the gold heart about one fingernail wide, about twice a bead's width and about one fifth of the wrist's width; about ten beads plus the clasp show across the front of the wrist; never chunky, never bold'. Drop the '15mm', 'peppercorn' and 'two and a half beads' heart sizing for worn frames; the real heart is about 1.9 bead widths. Ask for an average adult wrist with naturally proportioned fingers. If the Kathak read matters, ask again for the palm toward the camera. Accept only if bead/wrist is 0.14 or less (aim for 0.11).

fix: Reshoot. Replace the 'warm ivory handmade paper' with pale blush handmade paper or blush linen, and write 'pale ivory-pink, never cream, beige, sand or tan'. Drop the curtain and the dark wall, or make the background soft blush plaster. Make the props read as envelopes: blank, about 6x9 cm, with visible pointed flaps. Wrap the bracelet once around the bundle's short side like a ribbon, toggle closed on top and heart over the front edge. Keep the current bead and heart scale and the dried rosebud.
